notes: LibreTranslate has no user accounts, so a public instance is protected with its own API keys: key support is on (LT_API_KEYS) and every translation, detection and file request needs a valid key (LT_UNDER_ATTACK, the upstream switch that turns keyless use off completely). A request without a key gets 400 "Please contact the server operator to get an API key"; a wrong key gets 403. The language list and the web page itself open without a key.

The token on the first-run card is your API key (32 characters, 600 requests a minute). Send it as api_key in the JSON body or form of /translate, /detect and /translate_file. On every start the container writes it into the key database again, so it always works, even after a re-create.

Using the web page: open https://<domain>/, click the key icon at the top right and paste the token; the browser keeps it, and the page translates as you type. The page always shows upstream's notice that translation is limited to users with a valid API key; that is expected, and with the key set it translates.

More keys, for other people or apps: run ltmanage keys --api-keys-db-path /app/db/api_keys.db add 120 in a shell inside the container (the app page's Command-line access card shows how to open one); it prints a new key allowed 120 requests a minute. ltmanage keys --api-keys-db-path /app/db/api_keys.db lists them, and the same command with remove <key> deletes one. A removed key can keep working for up to 30 seconds, because each worker caches key lookups. Keys live in the keys volume on /app/db.

Languages: only the panel's 8 languages are loaded (LT_LOAD_ONLY=en,es,de,fr,pt,ja,ru,hi), which keeps the first download and the memory use small. To add one, append its code (for example it, nl, zh, ko) to LT_LOAD_ONLY in the panel's environment editor and restart: LT_UPDATE_MODELS is on, so each start fetches upstream's model index, downloads models for new languages and updates changed ones. Models already on the volume are not downloaded again. The 8 languages are 16 models (to and from English), about 2 GB on disk; every extra language adds about 250 MB on disk and more memory once it is used, so raise the memory limit if you add several.

The models download from the Argos Translate index on the first start, so the server needs outbound internet access, and the first start downloads about 1.5 GB: the panel shows the app as running within a minute, but the site answers 502 for 3 to 5 minutes until the models are in place. Later starts answer in about 20 seconds. They live in the models volume on /home/libretranslate/.local and survive restarts and re-creates.

It runs on the CPU (the -cuda image is not used). LT_THREADS=2 runs two worker processes; each one loads the models it uses, so more workers answer more requests at once but need more memory. With every language pair used in both workers, memory reached 1.5 to 1.75 GB of the 2g floor (idle it is under 300 MB); if you add languages, raise the memory limit or set LT_THREADS to 1.
The image runs as its own unprivileged user (uid 1032).

Verified live on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (RC-47): created from the 1-Click Recipes tab, Running in 48 s on both; the models downloaded in 157 s (26.04) and 261 s (24.04), 16 models and 2.0 GB, and the site answered 200 after 189 s and about 300 s. With the first-run token, Hello world en→es returned Hola mundo, and en→ja, hi, ru, de, fr, pt and es→de all translated; without a key /translate and /detect answered 400, with a wrong key 403; /languages listed the 8 languages; the web page translated after the key was set from its key icon; ltmanage added a 120-a-minute key that worked and was refused after removal; a restart and a forced re-create answered again in about 20 s with no model downloaded again and the same token. Idle 160 to 270 MiB of 2g; with every pair used in both workers 1.5 to 1.75 GB, never OOM-killed. Every image ref below is in its tested list.
